Over the years, it has been inconsistent, and challenging to decide upon at an individual student level.
The recent addition of NFS 550 to the graduate curriculum has resulted in a course option that meets the needs of NFS graduate students.
It covers important concepts such as study design, appropriate data interpretation, and dissemination.
The course also includes hands-on learning with data analyses and understanding the nuances of big data.
With an emphasis on critical thinking, this course also exposes learners to a diverse array of scientific literature.
By including this course in the NFS graduate curriculum, it allows consistent and solid training of our MS students.

As with many other fields, nutrition has become increasingly multidisciplinary.
Thus, students should gain multidisciplinary learning during their graduate training.

FACULTY SENATE APRIL 15, 2021 REFERENDUM 2020-2021 - APRIL 2021 On April 15, 2021, the Faculty Senate voted in favor of amending Articles III, IV and V of the Constitution of the Faculty Senate to modify the Faculty Senate membership and apportionment system. In accordance with Article VII, 1 and 2 of the Constitution, the amendment was subject to ratification "by an affirmative vote of two-thirds of the General Faculty, excluding abstentions." The referendum of the General Faculty was conducted from April 26, 2021 until May 3, 2021 via electronic ballots. The results of the referendum are: Affirmative votes 310 Negative votes 48 Abstentions 3 Total votes 361 Total votes, excluding abstentions 358 Excluding abstentions, of the votes cast, 87% were affirmative: the amendment has been ratified. The Faculty Senate will now forward this Bill to President Dooley for his approval. Once it is approved, the modified Faculty Senate membership and apportionment system will take effect for the Spring 2022 apportionment calculations and college elections.
